lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- I See It Differently
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Roberto Saraiva | Lesson 13 -- I See It Differently
lesson.grammar_point: softeners for polite disagreement: I see your point but, I'm afraid, I'm not sure, maybe we could

listenings.text: In my workshops, I always ask one question. When you disagree with a client, what do you want to keep? Most people say: my price. That is the wrong answer. You want to keep two things: the deal and the relationship. So here is a simple rule. Disagree with the idea, never with the person. Do not say: you are wrong. Say: I see your point, but the numbers say something different. Then look for the common ground. What do both sides want? Start there, and the rest of the conversation is easier. And one more thing. Never push back without an alternative. If you only say no, the other side has nowhere to go. If you say no, and then, maybe we could try this, you are still negotiating. A good no always comes with a next step.

Hi, Roberto, it's Paula. I read your proposal for Lakeshore, the two percent now and two percent in October. I see your point, and I know we need this order. But I'm not sure October works for us. Our new costs start in July, not in October, so for three months we lose money on every box. I'm afraid the finance team is going to push back. Maybe we could do it a little differently. What if the second increase starts in August? It is still a compromise for Megan, and we do not lose three months. It is a small change, but I think it is important. Can we talk before you call her on Monday? I am free after two.
